tools.name: show_in_component_code
tools.description: Shows a React component in the chat in Component Code: a live preview beside the code that uses it. Each string, number and boolean in the code becomes a control the reader can change. Use it when someone asks to show a component in Component Code, or to see, preview or try one.

source.description: The component's module in TSX. It may import only from 'react'. Its exports, the default one by its function's name, are what `code` can name. For each value the reader can change by using the component, such as `checked`, `open` or `value`, take a matching `onCheckedChange`, `onOpenChange` or `onValueChange` prop and call it with the new value. Component Code passes it, so the change shows in the code. Keep state of its own only for when the prop is missing.

code.description: How the component is used, in JSX: elements, props and text only, with no hooks, calls or conditions. It is shown as code and rendered as the preview. Each string, number and boolean in it becomes a control.

file.description: The file named in the code's tab, such as `Card.tsx`.

controls.description: How a prop is changed, by its name or by `Element.prop`: a list of options, `{ min, max, step }` for a number, or `false` to keep it as written.

tools.name: show_html_in_component_code
tools.description: Shows HTML, CSS and JS running in the chat in Component Code: the page beside its code, with a tab for each file. The values named in `controls` become controls the reader can change. Use it when someone asks to show HTML, CSS, JS, a canvas or an SVG in Component Code, or for an experiment without React.

files.description: The files by name, such as `index.html`, `style.css` and `script.js`, each in its own tab. They run together as one page in a sandboxed frame: the HTML is the page's body, with the CSS in a style element and the JS in a script element after it. The page cannot load anything from the network, so draw with canvas, SVG or the DOM.

controls.description: The values the reader can change, by name: an attribute, as `r` or `circle.r`, a CSS property or custom property, as `--speed`, or a JS `const` set to a number, string or boolean. Each takes `true`, a list of options, or `{ min, max, step }` for a number. CSS changes apply as the reader drags, while HTML and JS run the page again, so a script that reads custom properties each frame follows along.

tools.name: play_while_you_wait
tools.description: Shows Orbit, a small one-button game, in the chat for the reader to play while you work. It returns at once and the game keeps running, so call it first and carry on with the task. Use it only when someone asks for a game, or for something to do while they wait.
